title: Largest plus smallest neighbour factor
W: Add the largest prime factor of n to the smallest prime factor of n + 1. Tested starts reach 5 → 7 → 9 or 22 → 34. Prove all do.
M: For $f(n)=P(n)+p(n+1)$, with $p$ the least prime factor, prove every orbit with $n\ge3$ reaches $(5,7,9)$ or $(22,34)$.

title: Mixed divisor-sum map
W: Add the sum of distinct prime factors of n to the largest prime factor of n + 1. Tested starts reach 14, 21, or loops through 5, 10, 31 or 82. Prove these are the only fates.

title: The parity-switch prime map
W: For even n add P(n) and P(n+1); for odd n add P(n) and P(n−1). Every tested start falls into one nine-step loop through 5. Prove all do.
M: For $f(n)=P(n)+P(n+(-1)^n)$, prove every orbit with $n\ge3$ reaches $(5,7,10,16,19,22,34,24,8)$.

title: Factor plus next divisor-sum
W: Map n to P(n) plus the sum of distinct primes dividing n + 1. Every tested start falls into 16 → 19 → 26. Prove all do.
M: For $f(n)=P(n)+\mathrm{sopf}(n+1)$, prove every orbit with $n\ge2$ reaches $(16,19,26)$.

title: Square-sum Hamiltonian paths from 1
W: Count the ways to line up 1 to N with neighbours summing to squares, starting from 1. Show this count grows faster than any polynomial.
M: Let $h(N)$ be the number of Hamiltonian paths of $S_N$ starting at vertex $1$. Prove $\log h(N)/\log N\to\infty$.

title: Square-sum K4s
W: Find four distinct positive integers where every pair sums to a square, with the least largest element, and show infinitely many such families have polynomial size relations.
M: Prove there are infinitely many $\{a,b,c,d\}$ with all six pairwise sums square and $\max\le C\min^{A}$ for fixed $C,A$.

title: Permanent of the prime-sum matrix
W: Find the asymptotic count of perfect matchings between odd and even numbers up to 2n whose sums are all prime.
M: Determine $\log\mathrm{per}(M_n)$ to $o(n)$ where $M_n=(\mathbf 1[2i-1+2j\text{ prime}])_{i,j\le n}$.

title: Optimal square-sum circle gaps
W: Among all arrangements of 1 to N in a circle where neighbours sum to squares, minimise the largest difference between neighbours. Find the order of the minimum.
M: Determine the order of $\min_{C}\max_{i}|v_{i+1}-v_i|$ over Hamiltonian cycles $C$ of $S_N$.

title: Continued fraction of the P-constant
W: Show the constant formed by largest prime factors as continued fraction digits is transcendental.
M: Prove $[0;P(2),P(3),P(4),\dots]$ is transcendental.

title: Two small factors and one large
W: Add the smallest prime factors of n and n + 1 to the largest prime factor of n + 2. Every tested start falls into one seven-step loop through 16. Prove all do.
M: For $f(n)=p(n)+p(n+1)+P(n+2)$, prove every orbit with $n\ge2$ reaches $(16,22,28,36,58,66,86)$.

title: The 2n+3 map
W: Map n to P(2n + 3) + P(n). Orbits can climb past seven million before falling, yet every tested start ends in loops through 6, 9 or 50. Prove all do.

title: The P(n)+P(n+2)−1 map
W: Map n to P(n) + P(n+2) − 1. Tested starts reach 4 or loops of length 18, 11 and 4. Prove these are all.
M: For $f(n)=P(n)+P(n+2)-1$, prove every orbit reaches $\{4\}$, the 18-cycle through $23$, the 11-cycle through $7$, or $(223,227,455,469)$.

title: Unbounded excursions in prime maps
W: For n ↦ P(n) + P(n+1), show some orbits climb above their starting value by any factor you like.
M: Prove $\sup_n\max_k f^k(n)/n=\infty$ for $f(n)=P(n)+P(n+1)$.

title: Prime-sum Kayles
W: Same game on the prime-sum graph: take numbers so that no two taken numbers sum to a prime. Decide who wins.
M: Determine the outcome of the independent-set game on the prime-sum graph on $[N]$ for all large $N$.

title: Large girth subgraphs of S_N
W: Find the most edges a subgraph of the square-sum graph can have with no cycle shorter than 6.
M: Determine the order of $\mathrm{ex}(S_N,\{C_3,C_4,C_5\})$.

title: Largest-factor tribonacci
W: Repeatedly add the largest prime factors of the last three terms. Show the sequence is always eventually periodic.
M: For $a_{n+3}=P(a_{n+2})+P(a_{n+1})+P(a_n)$, prove eventual periodicity for every start in $\mathbb{N}_{\ge2}^3$.

title: Spanning-tree entropy of the spectre tiling
W: Find the growth rate of the number of spanning trees of large spectre-tiling patches, and show it is not a rational multiple of Catalan's constant.
M: Prove $\lim\frac{\log\tau(G_R)}{|V(G_R)|}=h$ exists for spectre patches and $h/G\notin\mathbb{Q}$, $G$ Catalan's constant.

title: Matrices with prime entries and unit determinant
W: Count 2 by 2 matrices with all four entries prime and determinant 1 or −1, with entries up to X.
M: Determine the asymptotics of $\#\{(p,q,r,s)\in\mathbb{P}^4\cap[1,X]^4: ps-qr=\pm1\}$.

title: Prime Markov triples
W: Show only finitely many Markov triples consist of three primes, or infinitely many.
M: Decide whether infinitely many solutions of $x^2+y^2+z^2=3xyz$ have $x,y,z$ all prime.

title: Seven-free Markov numbers
W: Show infinitely many Markov numbers have no digit 7.
M: Prove infinitely many Markov numbers $m$ satisfy $7\notin m$ (decimal).

title: Apollonian seven-free curvatures
W: In the Apollonian packing (−1, 2, 2, 3), show infinitely many circles have curvature with no digit 7, and count them.
M: Prove $\#\{k\le X:k\in\mathcal{K},7\notin k\}=X^{\log_{10}9+o(1)}$ for the $(-1,2,2,3)$ packing.

title: Largest factor of p² + p + 1 small
W: Show infinitely many primes p have P(p² + p + 1) < p.
M: Prove $\#\{p\le x:P(p^2+p+1)<p\}\gg\pi(x)$.
